title: PRIMES-USA Year-Long Math Research
description: Free year-long distance research program pairing US high school sophomores and juniors with MIT mentors on unsolved problems in pure math, theoretical CS, and computational biology.
eligibility: Completely free academic research mentorship with no stipend or employer-employee relationship, so it is not employment under H4 rules.

title: Research Science Institute (RSI)
org: Center for Excellence in Education / MIT
description: Six-week residential summer program at MIT combining STEM coursework with a five-week individual research project under a scientist mentor. Admits about 100 students worldwide.
eligibility: Cost-free academic research program with no stipend or wages paid to students; educational mentorship, not employment.

title: Summer Science Program (SSP)
description: Five-week residential research immersion where teams of three complete an original project in astrophysics, biochemistry, genomics, or cell biology on a host college campus.
eligibility: Tuition-based academic program (need-based aid available) with no stipend paid to participants, so no work authorization is implicated.

title: Aspiring Scholars Directed Research Program
description: Nonprofit pre-collegiate research institute where grades 9-12 students join faculty-mentored lab groups in chemistry, biomedical science, CS, engineering, or astrophysics.
eligibility: Fee-based academic research mentorship at a nonprofit with no compensation to students; coursework-style research, not employment.

title: BU RISE Internship & Practicum
description: Six-week summer program for rising seniors doing 40 hrs/week of independent lab research with a BU faculty mentor, concluding with a poster symposium.
eligibility: Despite the word 'internship', this is a tuition-paying academic program with no stipend or wages, so it is not employment.

title: Garcia Center Summer Research Program
description: Seven-week interdisciplinary research program in polymers and materials science where high schoolers join labs working on drug delivery, energy storage, and materials design.
eligibility: Tuition-based university research program with no stipend paid to high school participants, so no work authorization is required.

title: Zooniverse Citizen Science Research
description: Free platform hosting hundreds of active research projects where volunteers classify galaxies, transcribe field notes, and annotate wildlife imagery. Contributions have been credited in peer-reviewed papers.
eligibility: Unpaid, open-access citizen science contribution with no compensation of any kind and no employment relationship.

title: NASA Citizen Science Projects
description: Directory of NASA-sponsored volunteer science projects covering exoplanet hunting, aurora observation, and asteroid searches. Volunteers have been named as co-authors on NASA-affiliated papers.
eligibility: Volunteer scientific contribution to federally funded research with no payment, stipend, or award of any kind.

title: Publish in the Journal of Emerging Investigators
description: Open-access, peer-reviewed journal founded by Harvard graduate students that publishes original middle and high school research, with detailed reviewer feedback through revision.
eligibility: Academic publishing with no fees paid in either direction and no employment relationship.

title: Idealist Remote Volunteer Opportunities
description: The largest US nonprofit volunteer board, with a remote filter covering tutoring, translation, research, graphic design, and web support roles.
eligibility: Genuine unpaid nonprofit volunteering. Caution: some listings offer stipends or are internships — filter strictly to unpaid roles at 501(c)(3) nonprofits.

title: Points of Light Virtual Volunteering
description: National volunteer-matching platform with a virtual filter spanning skills-based work like data entry, social media, graphic design, and translation for nonprofits.
eligibility: Unpaid nonprofit volunteering that supplements rather than displaces paid staff. Caution: skip listings offering stipends, gift cards, or incentives.

title: Learn To Be Volunteer Online Tutor
description: Nonprofit providing free 1-on-1 online tutoring in math and reading to underserved K-12 students, matching volunteers with a student on its own virtual whiteboard.
eligibility: Strictly unpaid volunteer tutoring for a nonprofit — permissible because no compensation is received. Paid tutoring would NOT be permissible on H4.

title: UPchieve Volunteer Academic Coach
description: On-demand free tutoring nonprofit where volunteers get alerts when a low-income student needs help in math, science, or college essays and answer whenever available.
eligibility: Explicitly '100% powered by volunteers' with zero compensation; unpaid tutoring for a nonprofit is permissible H4 activity.

title: Schoolhouse.world Peer Tutor
description: Nonprofit peer-tutoring platform where high schoolers certify in a subject then run free small-group sessions worldwide, earning verified tutoring-hour records.
eligibility: All programs are free and tutors are unpaid volunteers; no wages, stipends, or gift cards are involved.

title: Smithsonian Digital Volunteer Transcriber
description: Volunteers transcribe handwritten field notebooks, specimen labels, and diaries from Smithsonian museums to make them searchable. Transcriptions are credited and published.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer work for a federal trust institution with no compensation; a long-established public crowdsourcing program open to anyone.

title: By the People Crowdsourced Transcription
description: Library of Congress program where volunteers transcribe and tag digitized manuscripts, letters, and historical papers to improve accessibility and searchability.
eligibility: Unpaid public-service volunteering for a federal cultural institution with no compensation and no displacement of paid staff.

title: LibriVox Volunteer Reader / Proof-Listener
description: All-volunteer project recording public-domain books into free audiobooks; volunteers read chapters, proof-listen to recordings, or help with cataloging.
eligibility: Entirely volunteer-run project with no payment to anyone and output donated to the public domain.

title: Distributed Proofreaders for Project Gutenberg
description: Volunteers proofread a page at a time of scanned public-domain books to convert them into free Project Gutenberg e-books, starting on a guided track with mentor feedback.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer contribution to a nonprofit public-domain library with no compensation and no paid-worker displacement.

title: First Contributions Open-Source Onboarding
description: A hands-on tutorial repository walking complete beginners through forking, branching, and opening a real merged pull request, then pointing to beginner-friendly projects.
eligibility: Voluntary uncompensated contribution to public open-source software; no employer, no contract, no payment.

title: Good First Issue Contribution Finder
description: Curated index of popular open-source repositories filtered to issues tagged for first-time contributors, searchable by language. Useful for building a public GitHub history.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer contribution to public software projects with no compensation, bounty, or employment relationship.

title: Up For Grabs Open-Source Task Directory
description: Directory listing hundreds of open-source projects that maintain curated newcomer-friendly tasks, filterable by language, ranging from documentation fixes to feature work.
eligibility: Purely volunteer code and documentation contribution. Caution: avoid any listed project offering paid bounties for issues.

title: Humanitarian OpenStreetMap Volunteer Mapper
description: Volunteers trace buildings, roads, and waterways from satellite imagery to build open map data used by disaster-response and public-health organizations.
eligibility: Unpaid humanitarian volunteering producing open data for a nonprofit; no compensation and no displacement of paid staff.

title: Wikimedia New Developers Program
description: Official onboarding path for volunteers contributing code to MediaWiki, Wikipedia gadgets, bots, and tools, with curated good-first-tasks and assigned mentors.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer contribution to a nonprofit's open-source software. Caution: do NOT apply to Wikimedia's paid Outreachy/GSoC tracks.

title: Hack Club Open-Source Community
description: Nonprofit network of teen-run coding clubs whose members ship open-source projects, contribute to Hack Club's public repositories, and run free hackathons.
eligibility: Free nonprofit youth community with unpaid project work. Caution: some programs distribute hardware grants or travel stipends — decline cash or cash-equivalent awards.

title: MAA American Mathematics Competitions
description: The primary US high school math competition and the qualifying path to AIME, USA(J)MO, and the Math Olympiad Program. AMC 10A/12A is Nov 5, 2026; 10B/12B is Nov 13, 2026.
eligibility: Academic examination with recognition-only awards and no cash prizes, so no compensation or employment is involved.

title: USA Computing Olympiad Contests
description: Free online algorithmic programming contests from December through March across Bronze, Silver, Gold, and Platinum divisions, with hundreds of hours of free training material.
eligibility: Free academic programming competition with no entry fee and no cash prizes; division promotion is the only award.

title: USA Biology Olympiad (USABO)
description: Two-round national biology examination selecting National Finalists and the four-student US team for the International Biology Olympiad. Administered through registered schools.
eligibility: Academic olympiad awarding medals and team selection rather than money; participation involves no compensation.

title: U.S. National Chemistry Olympiad
description: Multi-tiered chemistry competition from ACS local-section exams in March through the National Exam in April and a study camp selecting the US international team.
eligibility: Academic olympiad with medal and team-selection awards only, involving no payment or employment.

title: Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair
description: The world's largest pre-college science competition, reached by first winning an affiliated local or state fair; finalists present original research in 22 categories.
eligibility: Academic science-fair competition. Caution: top finishers receive scholarship and prize awards — confirm with an immigration attorney before accepting any cash award.

title: Congressional App Challenge
description: Free nationwide coding competition where students build an original app solo or in teams of up to four and submit it to their congressional district. Winning apps are displayed in the Capitol.
eligibility: Free-to-enter competition whose award is recognition and Capitol display rather than money.

title: Wharton Global High School Investment Competition
description: Free ten-week team competition where students act as investment advisors for a fictional client, manage a simulated portfolio, and write a strategy report judged on research quality.
eligibility: Free academic competition using a simulated portfolio with no real money and no cash prize.

title: National Economics Challenge
description: The largest US high school economics competition, with team exams in micro, macro, and international economics progressing from state to national rounds.
eligibility: Academic subject competition run by a nonprofit. Caution: national finalists may receive scholarship awards — academic prizes, not employment income.

title: picoCTF Cybersecurity Competition
description: Free capture-the-flag cybersecurity competition and year-round practice gym covering reverse engineering, cryptography, web exploitation, and forensics.
eligibility: Free university-run educational competition. Caution: top-scoring US teams in some years receive cash prizes — verify any monetary award first.

title: freeCodeCamp Developer Certifications
description: Free self-paced curriculum granting verifiable certifications in responsive web design, JavaScript algorithms, data analysis with Python, and machine learning.
eligibility: Free self-study coursework from a nonprofit with no payment in either direction; education, not employment.

title: CS50x: Introduction to Computer Science
description: Harvard's flagship intro CS course, free and self-paced through eleven weeks of C, Python, SQL, and web development plus a final project, ending in a free certificate.
eligibility: Free open courseware with a free completion certificate; purely academic study with no compensation.

title: Kaggle Learn Micro-Courses
description: Free hands-on micro-courses in Python, pandas, data visualization, machine learning, SQL, and deep learning, each run in an in-browser notebook with a certificate.
eligibility: Free online coursework with completion certificates. Caution: Kaggle also hosts cash-prize competitions — take only the free courses.

title: Cisco Networking Academy Courses & Badges
description: Free self-enroll courses including Python Essentials, Introduction to Cybersecurity, Networking Basics, and Data Analytics Essentials, each awarding a Credly digital badge.
eligibility: Free self-study courses with digital badge credentials; education only, with no wages or employer relationship.

title: IBM SkillsBuild for High School Students
description: IBM's free learning platform with a dedicated high school catalog covering AI fundamentals, cybersecurity, cloud, data analysis, and design thinking, awarding digital credentials.
eligibility: Free educational platform issuing digital credentials, with no employment, stipend, or compensation attached.

title: HubSpot Academy Free Certifications
description: Free certification courses in digital marketing, content marketing, SEO, email marketing, and sales, each ending in a graded exam and a shareable certificate.
eligibility: Free online coursework and certification exams with no cost and no compensation; strictly skill-building, not work.

title: Google Cloud Skills Boost Badges
description: Hands-on lab-based learning paths in cloud infrastructure, data engineering, and generative AI that award verifiable skill badges after completing a challenge lab.
eligibility: Educational lab coursework issuing skill badges, with no compensation. Caution: some labs require credits — use free-tier or student credit offers.

title: DemocracyLab Tech-for-Good Projects
description: Volunteer-run platform matching skilled volunteers to 300+ tech-for-good projects needing front-end and back-end developers, UI/UX designers, QA testers, and writers.
eligibility: Unpaid skills-based volunteering for social-impact projects. Caution: projects set their own age requirements, and any offering payment should be avoided.

title: Open Source Design Volunteer Board
description: Community-run board listing design work needed by open-source projects, including logo design, UI/UX, and branding, with volunteer and paid listings labeled separately.
eligibility: Caution: this board mixes paid and volunteer listings — only listings explicitly marked 'volunteer' are H4-permissible. Never accept a paid engagement.

title: TED Translators Volunteer Subtitler
description: Volunteers transcribe and translate TED and TED-Ed talks into other languages, working through review with experienced language coordinators before subtitles go live.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer translation for a nonprofit media organization with public credit as the only recognition.

title: Bookshare Accessible Book Volunteer
description: Volunteers scan, proofread, and format books into accessible digital formats for readers with dyslexia, blindness, and other print disabilities, working remotely at their own pace.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteering for a nonprofit accessibility organization, supplementing rather than replacing paid staff.

title: CoderDojo / Code Club Volunteer Mentor
description: Volunteer-run free coding clubs for children ages 7-17 where mentors help young learners build Scratch, Python, and web projects using a free curriculum.
eligibility: Unpaid volunteer mentoring at a free nonprofit-run community club; all mentors are volunteers and no one is compensated.
